chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a person with a fracture who has splints upon him, or who has a wound—how should he act regarding wudu (ablution), and during ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah, and during the Friday ghusl (ritual bath)?

He عليه السلام said: 'He washes whatever the washing can reach of what is exposed, of that upon which there are no splints; and he leaves whatever is beyond that, which he is unable to wash. He should not remove the splints, nor should he meddle with his wound.'

key_terms.الْجَبَائِرُ: splints or bandages placed over an injured limb
key_terms.الْجِرَاحَةُ: a wound or injury on the body
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual washing of the body or a body part
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution) performed for ritual purity before salat (prayer)
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ghusl (ritual bath) required after janabah

ai.seo_question: How should a person with splints or wounds perform wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal ruling for a person with splints or wounds in wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath). He washes the accessible, uncovered parts and leaves what he cannot wash, without removing the splints or disturbing the injury.
